newsitem.title: INDIA: Big chance seen for Indian information technology.
newsitem.headline: Big chance seen for Indian information technology.

text.p: India has an opportunity to boost its share of world trade in a growing $400 billion information technology market, trade experts said on Monday.

Anwarul Hoda, deputy director-general of the Geneva-based World Trade Organisation (WTO), told an economic seminar organised by the World Economic Forum that India currently holds only 0.1 percent of the global information technology market.

Martin Posth, a board member of German car-maker Volkswagen AG and its president for the Asia-Pacific region, said India's intellectual resources and competitive engineering skills could stand out as a strategic point in luring foreign investment.
"In this area, I see the opportunity for a unique selling point (USP) in general," Posth said.

Referring to India's "Silicon Valley", Bangalore, he said there were other nations now competing with India with an advantage in cheap labour costs in fields like textile manufacturing, but India's computer skills could stand out.
Hoda said India had technical skills to absorb the latest technology in the world, needed to join a group of nations which have abolished import duties on computers and allied materials.
"Fast access to information technology at most competitive prices will help India to modernise," he said.

India needed appropriate laws to protect intellectual property, easier import of capital goods like machinery, macroeconomic stability and a big push in infrastructure to attract and retain foreign investment, Hoda said.
